definition-changed.flag: class | of a data item; external data
definition-changed.answer: Class object / category object-reference is the same Table 3 row in both (§2002:8.5.2.11 'An elementary data item explicitly or implicitly described as usage object-reference is of category object-reference'); the PB5625 usage-national question cannot reach a predefined object reference. 'external data' §2002:4 (4.81) 'Data that belongs to the run unit and may be accessed by any runtime element in which it is described' differs from 2023 3.79 only in 'may'/'can'. Scope unchanged.

definition-dropped.answer: §2002:4 (4.141) 'object reference: An explicitly- or implicitly-defined data item that contains a reference to an object'; 2023 moved the meaning to §2023:9.3.2 ('An object reference is an implicitly- or explicitly-defined data item containing an object reference value'), which adds uniqueness but names the same items. SR2 states EXCEPTION-OBJECT's implicit description; nothing in it depends on the wording. Scope unchanged.

held.flag: S1 (adopt-2002): its witness was refused at 2002 for the exception-object user word, which the rule names
held.answer: The refused witness is pb922_exception_object_user_word_85 (accept [85]): it uses EXCEPTION-OBJECT as an ordinary 1985 user word, which 2002 reserves as this predefined object reference (§2002:8.4.2.6), so its refusal at 2002 (COBOL2196/COBOL1694) is the 2002 behaviour, not evidence against SR2. SR2's 2002 witness is pb922_exception_object_reference (accept [2002]), which S1 ran at 2002: pass (adopt-2002/s1-run-classified.json).
